issues.description: Race condition on is_registered mutates shared LoRA state without locking
issues.detail: In _create_trtllm_generate_request, lora_config.is_registered is set to True after appending weights, but the TritonLoraConfig instance is shared across all requests for that LoRA. Two concurrent first-time requests can both see is_registered=False, race to send weights, or one may flip the flag before the engine has actually registered the LoRA, causing the second to omit weights and fail. Needs a lock or per-task registration confirmation.

issues.description: LoRA weights loaded from disk on every first request blocks the async event loop
issues.detail: np.load of model.lora_weights.npy and model.lora_config.npy is performed synchronously inside an async request path. For multi-GB adapters this stalls the FastAPI event loop and all concurrent requests. Weights should be preloaded at startup (during _parse_lora_configs) or loaded in a threadpool.

issues.description: Path traversal / unsafe join when reading LoRA paths from multi_lora.json
issues.detail: lora_path comes straight from user-controlled multi_lora.json and is joined with os.path.join without normalization or containment check. An attacker who can write that file (or supplies a relative ../.. path) can cause np.load to read arbitrary .npy files on the server filesystem. Validate that resolved paths stay within the model repository.

issues.description: Debug print and traceback dumps left in hot paths
issues.detail: print(f"backend: {backend}") inside the lora-config loop and print(traceback.format_exc()) in chat.py, completions.py, embeddings.py routers and in _parse_lora_configs will spam stdout for every request/model load. These look like debug leftovers; replace with logger.debug/exception or remove before merge.

issues.description: _get_lora_config return type annotation lies about Optional
issues.detail: _get_lora_config is annotated as returning TritonLoraConfig but returns None when lora_name is None or lora_configs is None. Also model_metadata.get(model_name) can return None and is dereferenced without check, raising AttributeError on unknown model_name. Annotate Optional[TritonLoraConfig] and handle missing metadata.

issues.description: lora_task_id numbering is per-call and not unique across models or restarts
issues.detail: _parse_lora_configs starts lora_task_id at 1 each invocation. If the function is called multiple times or for multiple TRT-LLM models in the same repo, task IDs collide, causing TRT-LLM to serve wrong adapter weights from its cache. Task IDs should be globally unique within the engine lifetime (e.g. hash of name+path or a process-wide counter).

review.summary: The PR adds TRT-LLM multi-LoRA support but the runtime registration logic has a real concurrency hazard: the shared TritonLoraConfig.is_registered flag plus synchronous np.load on the async request path will cause both correctness and latency problems under concurrent first-time requests. There are also security concerns around unvalidated lora paths read from multi_lora.json, non-unique task IDs, and several debug prints/traceback dumps that look like leftovers. Type annotations on the new helper are inaccurate and can mask a NoneType dereference for unknown models. Recommend addressing P0 issues before merge.
